answer_core:
The first problem is not to investigate the report or pick the reporting channel. The first problem is to preserve your legal options and avoid creating new risk before counsel reviews the facts.

Tonight, write down exactly what you saw, preserve your own notes, tell your spouse in broad strokes, and contact two or three whistleblower attorneys. Do not confront the partner, access systems unusually, investigate privately, or choose GC, audit committee, regulator, or external reporting yourself.

Use counsel to decide the channel. During intake, ask practical questions about when they recommend internal-first, audit-committee-first, or external-first paths and why.

Attend Wednesday normally. If the partner raises the encounter, keep the response narrow. Do not deny, elaborate, confront, investigate, or be alone with the partner if avoidable. Keep the first moves reversible.
